summary.text: Andrew Lanza is the Republican incumbent state senator for District 24, covering most of Staten Island, and has held the seat since 2007. A Staten Island lawyer and accountant, he was a Manhattan Assistant District Attorney and a New York City Council member before winning the Senate seat in 2006. He is Deputy Minority Leader and sits on the Judiciary and Rules committees.

paragraphs.text: Andrew Lanza was born in Brooklyn in 1964, grew up in Great Kills, Staten Island, and graduated from Monsignor Farrell High School in 1982.
He earned a B.S. in accounting from St. John's University and a J.D. from Fordham University School of Law in 1992.

He worked as a senior auditor at KPMG Peat Marwick and then as an Assistant District Attorney in the Manhattan office of Robert Morgenthau, and he later became general counsel partner of Mercury Securities LLC, a Wall Street software and trading firm; he describes his background as including accountant and business owner.

Lanza was first elected to the New York City Council (51st District) as a Republican in 2001 and was re-elected in 2003 and 2005; his Senate biography cites zoning laws he enacted on the Council to limit overdevelopment.
He was elected to the State Senate on November 7, 2006, succeeding the retiring John Marchi, and took office in 2007.
He serves as Deputy Minority Leader and sits on the Rules, Judiciary, Ethics and Internal Governance, and Cities 1 committees; he is a former chair of the Senate Codes Committee.

According to his Senate biography, Lanza created the I-STOP prescription drug monitoring database and led the effort to establish the 13th Judicial District, consisting solely of Richmond County (Staten Island).
The biography also says he lives in Great Kills with his wife, Marcele, a New York City public school teacher, and their three children.
